newsitem.title: UK: LCE coffee ends firm, focus on switches.
newsitem.headline: LCE coffee ends firm, focus on switches.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures reversed to end firmer across-the-board on Tuesday, dragged higher by a hefty spot premium and industry bargain hunting, traders said.
The spot September premium jumped on Tuesday to around $60 a tonne before settling at $53 a tonne at the close after touching a high of $49/$50 a tonne on Monday.
Traders said the premium had widened because it seemed the long-holder in September wanted to take delivery of the coffee.
"It may be insurance ahead of October - when new supply will come to the market," said one trader.
September may prove tight for spot supply.
But with the open interest on September at 2,401 lots on Tuesday and the uncovered said to be at some 2,200 lots, traders said a squeeze is unlikely.
"The spot premium is already attracting gradings," said another, noting that 31 originals were posted on Tuesday.
"Now if the premium moves much higher, it will attract more coffee," he added.
The Nov/Jan spread was also active on Tuesday with November going out to a premium of some $50 a tonne on Tuesday.
At the close on Tuesday the November contract was up $7 at $1,555 a tonne but off a high of $1,563 a tonne.
Volume on the exchange reached 3,146 lots.
